title: Daylight and Seasons
seo_title: Grade 1 Daylight and Seasons Worksheets: Long Summer Days, Short Winter Days
standard_text: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year.
meta_desc: Free grade 1 science worksheets on daylight and seasons (NGSS 1-ESS1-2): long summer days, short winter days, daylight graphs and sunset times. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Winter days are short. The pattern repeats every year.
body_html:
How to think about it

Daylight changes during the year.

  • Summer: long days.
  • Winter: short days.
  • The pattern repeats every year.
Example

Which month has more daylight, June or December?

Look at the bars.

Answer: June

Example

In which season does it get dark early?

Short days.

Answer: winter

Common mistakes

  • Thinking every day has the same daylight.
  • Thinking winter days are the longest.
  • Thinking the sun sets later in winter.

faq.a: In summer the sun rises earlier and sets later, so there are more hours of daylight.
In much of the United States, about 15 hours in June and about 9 hours in December.
Write down the sunset time once a month, or note if it is light or dark at the same time each evening.
